subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Projection Bias
description: A quick win: understand Projection Bias.

hook.text: Shoppers who grocery-shop while hungry buy 64% more junk food. They project current hunger onto future meals.

buildup.text: Projection bias means assuming your future preferences will match your current ones.

discovery.text: Loewenstein showed people overestimate how long current feelings will last. Happiness fades; misery fades.

twist.text: Gym memberships spike in January when motivation is high. By March, the mood fades but the contract remains.

climax.text: Before a big decision, ask: will I still feel this way in six months? If unsure, delay or add a cancellation option.

punchline.text: Today's feeling is a terrible forecast of tomorrow.

quiz.question: What is projection bias?
options: Projecting your feelings onto other people
Assuming future preferences will match current ones

details.summary: Projection bias causes people to assume their current preferences, emotions, and needs will persist into the future. Hungry shoppers overbuy groceries. Happy house hunters overlook winter problems when buying in summer. Current states are projected onto all future states.
details.whyItMatters: Projection bias leads to systematic planning errors because people believe their future selves will feel exactly as they do now. This drives overspending when happy, under-preparation when comfortable, and poor long-term decision-making.
takeaways: People project current emotional states onto their future selves
Hungry grocery shoppers buy more food than they will actually eat
Planning should explicitly account for how preferences change over time

faq.question: How does projection bias affect financial planning?
faq.answer: People in comfortable circumstances under-save because they project current comfort forward. People feeling deprived overcommit to future frugality they will not maintain. Both directions lead to plans that reflect current feelings rather than realistic future needs.

faq.question: What helps counteract projection bias in decision-making?
faq.answer: Make important decisions in a neutral emotional state. Recall similar past situations where your preferences changed. Build flexibility into plans that accommodates preference shifts. Use commitment devices for decisions you know you will regret reversing.
